what_it_does.name: seo-audit
what_it_does.summary: Instructions and seven reference documents for auditing the SEO of a website. The audit runs in priority order through crawlability and indexation, technical foundations, on-page optimization, content quality and authority, with added checklists for multilingual sites, local businesses, title tags and pages ranking in positions 8 to 20. The result is an audit report with an executive summary, findings with issue, impact, evidence, fix and priority, and a prioritized action plan. Use it when someone wants to audit or diagnose SEO, asks why traffic dropped or a page won't rank, or just says their SEO is bad.
tasks: audit crawlability, indexation and technical SEO
check Core Web Vitals, mobile-friendliness, HTTPS and URL structure
review title tags, meta descriptions, headings, images and internal linking
check hreflang, canonicals and sitemaps on multilingual and multi-regional sites
diagnose local SEO, Business Profiles, citations, reviews and location pages
move pages ranking in positions 8 to 20 onto page one and fix weak click-through
what_it_does.author_description: When the user wants to audit or diagnose SEO, or asks why traffic dropped, a page won't rank, or whether a setup like canonicals, hreflang, or redirects is right: technical SEO, indexing, Google updates, on-page and titles, Core Web Vitals, local SEO. Start here when someone just says their SEO is bad. For pages at scale, see programmatic-seo. For structured data, see schema. For AI search, see ai-seo.

risks.risk: Instructions embedded in the HTML, meta tags or copy of a fetched page reach the agent when it analyses the site.
risks.mitigation: an instruction to treat fetched pages as untrusted data and never follow embedded instructions, in place

risks.risk: A home-based business owner's private address becomes public when it is added to citations or JSON-LD markup.
risks.mitigation: instructions never to publish a hidden home address, in place

risks.risk: A review request that offers incentives, selects only happy customers or requires particular wording breaks Google's review policy.
risks.mitigation: a neutral example request and the rule against incentives, in place

risks.risk: A reply to a complaint exposes customer, medical, financial or job details.
risks.mitigation: instruction to offer a private contact path instead, in place

risks.risk: Profile edits, customer messages or directory submissions are made on the user's accounts when the agent acts under an existing authorization, with no way to undo stated.
risks.mitigation: a drafted plan does not itself authorize execution, in place

limitations: web_fetch and curl cannot reliably detect structured data, since JSON-LD injected by client-side JavaScript does not appear in static HTML.
Without access to a Business Profile, only a provisional plan with the evidence needed can be given.
Search Console data is limited by privacy thresholds and aggregation, and analytics counts by consent, blockers and tagging.
Schema validation does not guarantee rich-result display or a local-pack ranking change.
If two rounds of edits move nothing, the page is probably limited by intent mismatch or authority, which more on-page work won't fix.

known_problems.problem: no schema found with web_fetch or curl
known_problems.workaround: check with a browser tool, the Google Rich Results Test or a Screaming Frog export

known_problems.problem: Google shows a different title than the one written
known_problems.workaround: tighten the title and align it with the H1

known_problems.problem: a new page is not indexed after a few weeks
known_problems.workaround: check the causes in the Indexation section instead of resubmitting

known_problems.problem: no concrete reason a page ranks below the top three
known_problems.workaround: work on links with the link-building skill rather than a rewrite

known_problems.problem: Next.js alternates.languages omits the self-referencing xhtml:link
conflicting hreflang annotations in HTML and sitemap
known_problems.workaround: make the methods agree, since Google drops the conflicting pair
